facts.title: Professional overview
facts.text: Gino Odar is based in Lima, Peru. His professional background spans backend development, API integrations, production troubleshooting, and quality engineering. He speaks English, German, and Spanish. He is working toward applied AI systems and forward-deployed engineering roles, not claiming to have held those exact job titles.

facts.title: Backend engineering and APIs
facts.text: Gino has worked on Java and Spring Boot services, REST APIs, reporting and attribution workflows, advertising platform integrations, and issues involving service, data, and frontend boundaries. Kafka is part of his engineering toolkit; no specific production throughput or lead-architect ownership is claimed.

facts.title: Quality engineering and Playwright
facts.text: Gino has worked with Playwright for UI and end-to-end automation, regression testing, staging validation, reproduction of defects, and debugging flaky tests. His QA investigations span browser behavior, API responses, database records, and service logic. His toolkit also includes Selenium, JUnit, and Mockito.

facts.title: Infrastructure, data, CI/CD and observability
facts.text: His tooling includes OpenSearch, ClickHouse, PostgreSQL, MySQL, Docker, Linux, AWS tooling, Jenkins, Semaphore CI, New Relic, and Amazon CloudWatch. He has used New Relic and CloudWatch during investigations, and worked in delivery environments incorporating CI/CD and data infrastructure. The profile does not claim he designed all these systems.

facts.title: Frontend and mobile stack
facts.text: Gino has worked with TypeScript, JavaScript, React, Next.js, React Native, Node.js, and Express. Public work includes a full-stack React/TypeScript and Express/PostgreSQL prototype with provider abstractions and mock mode.

facts.title: AI development and learning focus
facts.text: Gino has participated in a collaborative LLM + Streamlit hackathon project and experimented with local LLM workflows using Ollama and Qwen. He is exploring Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Model Context Protocol (MCP), tool calling, agent orchestration, RAG, and evaluations. These topics are areas of development; the profile does not claim extensive production AI deployment experience.

facts.title: Academic and research projects
facts.text: Gino has worked on master's-level computer science coursework including a discrete-event simulation comparing queue scheduling strategies and a Python data-mapping assignment with SQLite and Bokeh. His repository documentation includes limitations and reproducible steps. His precise graduation status is not specified here.
